charts.title: Companies now spend more of the economy on tech than at the dot-com peak
charts.alt: Line chart of business spending on information processing equipment and software as a share of US GDP since 1947, reaching a record in Q2 2026 above the Q4 2000 dot-com peak.
charts.takeaway: Companies now spend a bigger share of the economy on tech than at the dot-com peak.
charts.note: Business spending on computers and software hit 5.05% of GDP in Q2 2026, above the 4.46% dot-com peak in Q4 2000.

charts.title: How a 3x fund loses on a round trip
charts.alt: Chart showing how a daily-reset 3x leveraged fund can end below its starting value after the underlying index goes down and back up.
charts.takeaway: If the index drops 10% and recovers, a 3x fund is still down about 7%.
charts.note: Hypothetical two-day example with a daily 3x reset, before fees: $100 becomes $93.33.

charts.title: Last week: the pros sold. The crowd bought 3x.
charts.alt: Chart contrasting hedge fund selling in Goldman's prime book with record retail inflows into the 3x leveraged semiconductor fund SOXL.
charts.takeaway: Last week hedge funds sold while retail investors poured a record $7B+ into SOXL, a 3x leveraged chip fund.

charts.title: $MSTR and Metaplanet could be cut from MSCI indexes
charts.alt: Chart comparing how much of Strategy's and Metaplanet's assets are bitcoin, with Strategy at about 94.5 percent and Metaplanet at about 97.9 percent.
charts.takeaway: Bitcoin makes up about 94.5% of Strategy's assets and about 97.9% of Metaplanet's, which is why MSCI is weighing whether they still count as operating companies.
